1-11.cost: A set of window guards or child-safety locks costs about ₹500–₹1,500 to buy and install, and the job takes about ten minutes.

1-14.inPlainWords: The test itself is very inexpensive. In the Qidong 30-year follow-up study, infants who received the hepatitis B vaccine at birth had an 84% lower risk of developing primary liver cancer and a 72% lower rate of carrying the hepatitis B virus than unvaccinated peers. An adult found to have no antibodies needs three doses over six months.
1-14.caveats: This recommendation is for adults who were never vaccinated as a child, or whose antibodies have waned. India added hepatitis B to the routine infant immunisation schedule only in 2011, so most adults born before that were not vaccinated at birth and should check their status rather than assume they are covered. The 84% cancer-risk reduction belongs to people immunised at birth; adolescents vaccinated later saw only a 21% fall in virus carriage. For an adult the aim is to prevent a new infection, not to reproduce that cancer benefit. Vaccination does nothing for someone already infected; they need regular follow-up with a hepatologist. Infection is confirmed when the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) test is positive, and a full panel tells you whether you are immune, infected or susceptible.

1-15.cost: A clinic visit and wound cleaning cost about ₹300–₹800. If a tetanus vaccine or immunoglobulin is needed, add about ₹1,000–₹5,000 depending on the product and the hospital.

1-6.inPlainWords: Do not push an electric scooter or e-bike into a stairwell or lift, and do not charge it inside your home. A lithium-ion battery can catch fire within seconds and fill a stairwell with toxic smoke, cutting off your only escape route. Charge at a designated outdoor point, use the charger supplied with the vehicle, and never leave a battery charging overnight.
1-6.benefit: The National Building Code and the state fire-safety rules require common areas and escape routes to stay clear. The BIS standard for lithium-ion batteries and chargers is a safety baseline; a cheap unbranded battery may not meet it. A charging fire in a lobby or stairwell is especially dangerous because smoke rises and the exit is blocked. Many apartment associations now ban indoor charging in their bye-laws.
1-6.cost: No direct cost. The inconvenience is walking to the designated charging point. A BIS-certified charger and battery cost more than an unbranded one.
1-6.caveats: Do not buy a modified battery or a generic charger. Do not charge a damaged battery. If a battery swells, heats up or smells, stop using it and take it to a service centre.
1-6.sources: Bureau of Indian Standards, lithium-ion battery standards. <https://www.bis.gov.in/>; National Disaster Management Authority, fire safety. <https://ndma.gov.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>

1-2.cost: A helmet costs from a few hundred rupees to a few thousand, depending on the standard it meets, and takes five seconds to put on each time.

1-3.cost: A smoke alarm costs a few hundred rupees and a carbon monoxide alarm a few thousand. After installation, the batteries need to be replaced once a year.

1-10.cost: A child car seat costs a few thousand rupees and lasts several years. It adds about one minute to each trip to buckle the child in.

1-12.cost: Life jackets cost from a few hundred to a few thousand rupees. Parents must also give constant attention to watching their children.

1-18.cost: An HPV test costs from about ₹1,000 at a private laboratory, and the sampling takes a few minutes. A woman with a negative result can be tested again only once every five years.

1-4.title: Replace the gas hose and regulator when they are due, never tamper with the piping yourself, and refuse unsolicited “safety” sales visits
1-4.cost: A compliant hose costs a few hundred rupees and a regulator rather more; a stove is replaced when the maker’s service life ends. The job takes one visit from an authorised mechanic, and the replacement date is printed on the hose itself.
1-4.inPlainWords: The rubber tube between an LPG cylinder and the stove hardens, cracks and leaks as it ages, and a leaking joint is the ordinary way a kitchen fire starts. In India the hose and the regulator carry a printed date and a replacement interval, and changing them on time is the owner’s job. Under the Gas Cylinders Rules, 2016, only cylinders and fittings approved by the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation may be used, the tubing has to be of the approved grade and kept short, and it should not be run through a wall or under a door. If you have piped natural gas instead, the connection and the internal line may be installed or altered only by the city gas distribution company authorised by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board; nobody else should touch it.
1-4.benefit: These rules exist because a perished hose, a worn regulator washer or a joint that was never checked can turn a small leak into a fire, and because a cylinder refilled or repaired outside the licensed system carries no test record. Replacing the hose and regulator at the interval printed on them, keeping the tube away from heat, and checking the joints with soap solution now and then removes the commonest failure points. No rule obliges you to buy a hose, a regulator, a stove or an alarm from your distributor or from anyone who turns up at the door.
1-4.caveats: People pose as gas inspectors, perform a perfunctory “check” and then sell self-closing valves, alarms or hoses at a mark-up. You may refuse, and you may complain to the distributor or to the oil marketing company. If you smell gas: shut the cylinder valve, open the doors and windows, do not switch any electrical switch on or off, including lights and exhaust fans, do not light a flame, and leave the house. Call the 24-hour emergency number printed on the cylinder or the consumer card — every oil marketing company runs an LPG emergency line — or the city gas distribution emergency number for piped gas, from outside. A headache, nausea or drowsiness in the house at the same time is carbon monoxide poisoning until proved otherwise; get everyone out and to a hospital. See Chapter 13.
1-4.sources: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board. <https://pngrb.gov.in/>; Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation, Gas Cylinders Rules, 2016. <https://peso.gov.in/>; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. <https://mopng.gov.in/>

1-5.title: Do not pick, buy or eat wild mushrooms; no folk test tells a poisonous one from a safe one
1-5.cost: No expense involved. The hard part is giving up a seasonal delicacy, and the argument with the relative who picked it.
1-5.inPlainWords: No Indian agency publishes a nationwide count of wild-mushroom poisonings, so any figure you read online is a partial tally. The pattern that does repeat is a household cooking one pot from a day’s picking and several people falling ill together, often hours later. Testing with a silver needle, cooking with garlic, assuming a mushroom is safe because insects have eaten it, or believing that only brightly coloured ones are toxic are all false tests.
1-5.benefit: The danger is not an upset stomach but liver and kidney failure. The species that carry amatoxins cause vomiting and diarrhoea that seem to settle after a day, and liver injury follows two or three days later — which is why people reach hospital too late. Cooking does not destroy amatoxins, and a mushroom that one adult has eaten without harm is not therefore safe for a child, a pregnant woman or an older adult. Identification turns on features most pickers cannot see, and species new to science are described every year, so there is no home test worth trusting.
1-5.caveats: If anyone has eaten a suspect mushroom, go to a hospital at once and take the leftovers, the trimmings, or photographs of what was picked and where. Do not wait for the stomach upset to pass: the quiet day that follows is part of the poisoning, not the end of it. Treatment differs by toxin, so identifying the species matters. “Local people know them” is not a safe assumption, and neither is any of the folk tests above.
1-5.sources: White J, Weinstein SA, De Haro L, et al. (2019). Mushroom poisoning: a proposed new clinical classification. Toxicon, 157, 53-65.; Indian Council of Medical Research. <https://www.icmr.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>

1-9.title: Do not speed or drive after drinking, keep off the phone, and pull over to rest when you are tired
1-9.cost: There is no direct cost. Driving a little slower adds a few minutes to a trip. The hard part is drinking less at a social gathering and leaving the phone alone. On a long drive, plan a break of at least 20 minutes every few hours.
1-9.inPlainWords: On average, every 1% rise in speed raises the chance of a fatal crash by about 4%. There is no blood alcohol level at which driving is safe. Handling a phone while driving makes a crash about 3.6 times more likely than attentive driving, and dialling raises it 12.2 times. A driver who is visibly tired runs about 3.4 times the crash risk.
1-9.benefit: The World Health Organization puts the speed relationship at a 1% rise in average speed producing a 4% rise in fatal crash risk, and reports that risk climbs from the lowest blood alcohol concentrations. WHO also reports that drivers using a phone are about four times more likely to crash than those who are not, and that hands-free sets offer little advantage. A naturalistic study with cameras in more than 3,500 vehicles compared 905 injury and property-damage crashes with baseline alert, attentive, sober driving: handling a handheld phone raised crash odds 3.6-fold, dialling 12.2-fold, texting or messaging 6.1-fold, reaching for the device 4.8-fold, browsing 2.7-fold and handheld conversation 2.2-fold. Observable fatigue and drowsiness raised crash risk 3.4-fold (odds ratio 3.4).
1-9.caveats: The 1% speed and 4% fatality ratio comes from traffic modelling, not from randomised trials. For alcohol, WHO describes an upward trend with no fixed harmless threshold. The phone and drowsiness odds ratios cover all injury and property-damage crashes, not fatal crashes alone, and the baseline was ideal attentive driving, which inflates the ratios a little. Indian law penalises drink-driving under section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and dangerous driving under section 184; it sets no statutory rest break for a private driver, so the four-hour guidance here is advice, not a legal rule. Commercial passenger and goods vehicles run to permit conditions and state rules, so if you drive for a living, check what your permit requires. If you are drowsy, pull over at a fuel station and sleep. Sedating antihistamines such as chlorpheniramine or diphenhydramine also impair driving markedly, as Chapter 34, Rule 12 sets out. Persistent drowsiness at the wheel with loud snoring is worth a sleep-apnoea assessment, described in Chapter 3, Rule 27.
1-9.sources: World Health Organization (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries>; Dingus TA et al. (2016). 1-45.cost: An anti-HCV antibody test costs a few hundred rupees at a private laboratory and is free or nominal at a government hospital under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme. If it is positive, an HCV RNA PCR test shows whether the infection is active. Treatment is a direct-acting antiviral taken as one tablet a day for 8 to 12 weeks, free at designated government hospitals under the same programme and available as low-cost generics in the private market. The real obstacle is that a person with no symptoms rarely thinks to be tested.

1-43.caveats: Grade B is assigned because while trials conclusively prove that direct inquiry causes no harm, trials cannot ethically measure reductions in completed suicides. Benefit magnitude is rated Low because it reflects surrogate endpoints (ideation frequency rather than absolute mortality counts). Most trial protocols utilized clinical interviews or standardized screening questionnaires rather than informal peer conversations, though clinical guidelines generalize this finding to friends and family. If someone confirms they are having suicidal thoughts, do not leave them unattended: stay with them, connect them immediately to a crisis helpline (Tele-MANAS on 14416, or 112 if it is an emergency), and remove access to lethal means (medications, sharp objects, chemicals), as outlined in Chapter 1, Rule 25. If they express intent to harm others or have active preparations underway, immediate emergency services or hospital evaluation is necessary, as described in Chapter 8, Rule 15. The interval between acute ideation and action is often mere minutes, as noted in Chapter 1, Rule 32. Primary beneficiaries are family members, partners, friends, and colleagues.
